shortcut_name: three-edge parity reduces to a triangle
evidence: deepseek-v4-flash: "for a in range(1, n + 1)" and iterates pairs of "neighbors"; gpt-oss-120b: "for a in range(n)" and "for b in nbr[a]"
affordance_in_statement: This selection of three logs is considered a valid proof if you collect all the personnel ID numbers recorded across the three chosen logs into a single list, every ID number present in this list must appear an even number of times.
removal_suggestion: There is no semantics-preserving removal: three distinct simple edges whose endpoint occurrences all have even parity are intrinsically exactly a 3-cycle. Only changing the task's parity condition or the number/type of selected logs would eliminate this affordance.

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: Recognizes that the required three logs form a triangle and searches pairs of neighbors for the third edge.
survivor_shortcuts.affordance: every ID number present in this list must appear an even number of times

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: Uses adjacency lists and bitsets to search for a triangle, exploiting the same even-degree characterization.

common_affordance: The parity condition on exactly three distinct simple incompatibility logs is equivalent to finding a triangle in the graph.

defeated_student_causes.why_failed: Its triangle search has excessive worst-case work, causing TLE on dense graphs under the given bounds.
It searches for a triangle as a likely valid case but does not correctly enforce the required lexicographically smallest output among all valid vertex groups.

recommended_edit: No semantics-preserving single edit can defeat both survivors: the triangle characterization is the structural core of the task. Defeating them would require changing the parity condition or changing the requirement from exactly three logs.
